ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=42^\circ$, $\angle C=68^\circ$, $AD$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$, $AE$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$. Find the degree measure of $\angle EAD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle B=42^\circ$ and $\angle C=68^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle BAC=180^\circ-68^\circ-42^\circ=70^\circ$\\
Since AE is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAE=70^\circ \div 2=35^\circ$\\
Since AD is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADB=90^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle DAC=90^\circ-\angle C=90^\circ-68^\circ=22^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle EAD=\angle EAC-\angle DAC=35^\circ-22^\circ=\boxed{13^\circ}$,\\
that is, the measure of $\angle EAD$ is $13^\circ$
